samples.summary: Whole-root JSON snapshot for `sheet` copies in-CRDT comment threads, contradicting the design doc's own Non-Goal
samples.evidence: `JSON_ROOT_TYPES = new Set(['sheet','slides','board'])` copies *every* root key verbatim (`for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(snapshot)) root[key] = value`). Spreadsheet comment threads live inside the Yorkie root, not in Postgres: `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:3-5` does `if (!ws.comments) ws.comments = {}` on the worksheet proxy (`root.sheets[tabId].comments`), storing thread bodies, author `{userId, username, photo}` and timestamps. So a copied sheet arrives carrying all of the source's comment threads and their authors — directly against docs/design/document-copy.md's Non-Goal "Collaboration state. Comments, share links, presence, and analytics are deliberately not carried over: a copy is a new document" and against the README entry's "no comments/share-links/history carried over". It is also inconsistent across types: the `doc` arm goes through `readDocsRoot`/`writeDocsRoot`, which does not carry `comments` (`packages/frontend/src/types/docs-document.ts:24` shows docs comments are root-level, and `docs-tree.ts` never reads/writes them), and `pdf` skips CRDT entirely — so comments survive a sheet copy but vanish on a doc/pdf copy.

samples.summary: `snapshotJsonRoot` re-implements the `unwrapJson` helper the same PR extracted into `yorkie/yorkie-json.ts`
samples.evidence: This PR moves slides-tree's private `unwrapJson` into a new shared module `packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-json.ts` ("detects the proxy shape and parses back to a plain JS value"), yet the copy service writes its own second unwrapper (`JSON.parse(doc.toJSON())` + `while (typeof value === 'string') JSON.parse(value)`) and never imports the shared one. Net effect: the extraction gains no new consumer (grep shows `unwrapJson` is still imported only by `slides-tree.ts`), so the refactor is unrequested churn while the duplication it was meant to remove is reintroduced in the new file.

samples.summary: Allowlist + silent `return` for unknown types diverges from the repo's "unknown document type throws" convention, so a future type ships silently-empty copies
samples.evidence: `if (!JSON_ROOT_TYPES.has(type)) return;` silently skips content copying for anything not in the hardcoded set. The canonical mapping module states the opposite contract: `packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-doc-key.ts:8-10` — "Any new document type must be added here; an unknown type throws so the mistake surfaces at request time instead of silently falling through". A ninth CRDT-backed type added later would produce copies with no content and no error, contradicting Goal "One action duplicates a document of any type with its full content". Deriving blob types (pdf/image/file) explicitly and throwing on unknown would match the existing pattern.

samples.summary: backend.md's Documents endpoint catalogue (the canonical per-endpoint permission-gate reference) is not updated with the new endpoint
samples.evidence: backend.md §"Documents (`/documents`)" enumerates every document endpoint with its guard/gate (`GET /documents/:id`, `POST /documents`, `PATCH /documents/:id`, `DELETE /documents/:id`) and states the manager tier rule around `resolveDocManager`. The PR adds `POST /documents/:id/copy` with a deliberately divergent gate (membership only, not manager) but documents it only in the new feature doc, leaving the canonical endpoint/gate list incomplete — exactly the place a reader checks when reasoning about the manager tier.

samples.summary: In-root title fields are copied verbatim, so a copy's in-document title can disagree with its `(copy)` row title
samples.evidence: The whole-root snapshot copies `meta.title` for slides (`packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:36`) and `writeDocsRoot`/`writeNoteRoot` carry whatever title the source root holds, while the Postgres row is renamed to `<title> (copy)`. The design doc's Naming section only discusses the row title, so the divergence is unaddressed; it appears cosmetic today since display uses the DB title.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. `document-copy.service.ts:27` puts `sheet` in `JSON_ROOT_TYPES`, and `:188-198` copies every root key verbatim onto the new document with no filtering (no strip/sanitize logic exists anywhere in packages/backend/src/document). Spreadsheet comment threads are stored in that same Yorkie root: `packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-document.ts:94-96` declares `Worksheet.comments`, `:147` seeds it, `:118` hangs worksheets off `sheets[tabId]`, and `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:3-6,71-81,20-24` writes thread bodies, authors (userId/username/photo) and timestamps through the CRDT proxy. So a copied sheet carries the source's comment threads and their authors. That directly contradicts the canonical design doc's Non-Goal `docs/design/document-copy.md:33-35` ("Comments, share links, presence, and analytics are deliberately not carried over"), the service's own docblock at `document-copy.service.ts:35-37`, and the index entry `docs/design/README.md:146` ("no comments/share-links/history carried over"). It is also inconsistent across types: the `doc` arm goes through `readDocsRoot`/`writeDocsRoot` (`document-copy.service.ts:134-152`) and `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts` contains no `comments` handling at all, while `pdf`/`image`/`file` skip CRDT entirely (`:176`) even though PDF comments are root-level (`packages/frontend/src/types/pdf-document.ts:11`). Unmet stated Non-Goal/acceptance criterion = major under this lens; nothing guards or overrides it.
